reproduce: # S0K1/S0K2 additionally need the official toolbox (gitignored, no redistribution licence) at shapeComp_17_12_2024/ and: pip install -e .[shapecomp]
python scripts/run_shape_benchmark.py --stage d1 --methods E0 E1 E3 S0K1 S0K2
python scripts/run_shape_benchmark.py --stage d2 d3 d4 --methods E0 E1 E3 S0K1 S0K2
python scripts/run_shape_benchmark.py --stage d5 --methods E0 E1 E3 S0K1 S0K2
# d5b re-analyses d5 (a) by stimulus pair; it reads the files above and never rewrites them
python scripts/run_shape_benchmark.py --stage d6 --methods E0 E1 E3 S0K1 S0K2

# d6-correct recomputes the d6 retrieval headline from the stored per-cell table -- rotated cells and 0-degree controls as separate views, Precision@K renamed, Recall@K added. It re-runs no inference and rewrites none of the files it reads.

arm_availability.E1: all stages (EarthGlyph's own 91-D descriptors, NOT ShapeComp)
arm_availability.S0: H1/H2 pairwise only, from the authors' published 22-D coordinates (the MDS projection of the ORIGINAL 109-descriptor ShapeComp space). Outputs only: cannot score MPEG-7 or any new shape, so S0 is absent from every retrieval stage.
arm_availability.S0K1: all stages. Official KerNet1 weights ACTUALLY RUN locally via the numpy port (h5py, no TensorFlow), on the original contour under the official input contract. Can score MPEG-7 and new shapes. Validated vs published KerNet1 outputs (Figure8 pairwise Spearman ~0.98). Not rotation/mirror invariant.
arm_availability.S0K2: all stages. Official KerNet2 weights ACTUALLY RUN locally via the numpy port. Validated essentially exact vs published KerNet2 outputs (H2 per-dim r ~0.998, pairwise Spearman ~0.999). Can score MPEG-7 and new shapes. Not rotation/mirror invariant.

metric_name_corrections.rule: a rename changes no measurement. It only stops a reader drawing a recall conclusion from a precision number, which is what the old label invited.
metric_name_corrections.precision_at_k: relevant share OF THE RETURNED list: hits / min(k, n_returned)
metric_name_corrections.recall_at_k: relevant share OF WHAT COULD STILL BE FOUND for that query and condition: hits / retained relevant candidates, a per-query denominator

human_rating_prediction.metric: Spearman, restated so positive = agreement with human dissimilarity
human_rating_prediction.ci: two-level bootstrap, pairs AND observers, 2000 replicates

target_removal_retrieval.caveat: precision@10 -- stored as class_recall_at_10 in d2_metrics.json, which is Precision@K under a wrong name, not a mistake in the number -- uses MPEG-7 object CATEGORIES, not human similarity. T2/T3 are the conditions of interest; T0/T1 are controls.

conditions.T2: query plus E0-defined rigid near-duplicates removed
conditions.T3: T2 plus structurally similar wrong-category hard distractors added

target_removal_retrieval.e1_normalizer_policy: The T3 gallery inherits the plain MPEG-7 E1 normalizer, so adding distractors is the only variable. e1_normalizer_drift_if_refitted in d2_metrics.json records what a refit would have changed.

structure_probes.caveat: constructed roles, NOT validated human truth

transform_stability.metric: Jaccard overlap of Top-10 with the untransformed query, per transform

rotation_stress_agreement.study: one member of every rated H1 pair turned by each stress angle (a)
rotation_stress_agreement.metric: agreement with the published human dissimilarity, restated positive; rotation is the only variable and the human ground truth is shared by all arms

rotation_stress_retrieval.study: each D4 query turned by each stress angle against the stratified gallery (b)
rotation_stress_retrieval.metric: mean Top-10 overlap with the untransformed ranking over the rotated angles

rotation_stress_agreement_grouped.study: CP7-B re-analysis of rotation_stress_agreement: identical point estimates, uncertainty resampled by rated stimulus pair instead of by row
rotation_stress_agreement_grouped.why: d5 stacked 7 rotated angles onto each of 250 rated pairs and resampled the resulting 1750 rows independently, which counts one stimulus seven times as seven independent observations and makes every interval too narrow
rotation_stress_agreement_grouped.sampling_unit: the rated stimulus pair (250 pairs), not the row; 1750 rows = 250 pairs x 7 rotated angles and resampling rows independently understates the interval
rotation_stress_agreement_grouped.angle_factor: fixed: the rotation angles are a pre-declared design set and are never resampled, so inference is over stimuli and observers only
rotation_stress_agreement_grouped.angle_factor_sensitivity: random: the rotation angles are themselves drawn with replacement, so the interval also covers 'some other set of angles of the same size'

reproduction_of_committed_values.note: the naive (row-as-independent) bootstrap re-run from the stored CSV reproduces every committed d5 point estimate and CI, so the grouped numbers below are directly comparable to them

rotation_stress_agreement_grouped.ci: grouped two-level bootstrap (pairs + observers) with a shared replicate stream across arms; the angle-randomised interval is a sensitivity, not the headline
rotation_stress_agreement_grouped.paired_difference_convention: key "A|B" stores score(B) - score(A) on the agreement scale, so a positive value means the arm after the pipe is better; the mirrored reading is published beside it under an explicitly named field rather than left to the key order
assumptions: rotating one member of a pair does not change how the *human observers* rated that pair, so the published rating is reused for every angle; this is an assumption carried over from d5, not new human data — no rotated pair was ever re-rated
the seven rotated angles are a fixed design set (headline); treating them as a random sample of angles widens the intervals further and is reported as a sensitivity, not as the headline
the rating panel is exchangeable across stimuli, so one observer draw is applied per replicate for every arm

superseded_file.relation: this stage replaces that file. No magnitude changes: the point estimates, intervals and widths are re-derived from the same stored CSV with the same seed, and the only difference is that each paired contrast now publishes both readings under direction-named fields, so any number quoted from the superseded file is still present here as agreement_first_minus_second

rotation_wrappers_agreement.study: goal A: one member of every rated H1 pair turned by a frozen random stress angle; the wrapper decides the pose, the human ground truth is shared
rotation_wrappers_agreement.metric: agreement with the published human dissimilarity, restated positive; interval resampled by rated pair (CP7-B scheme), never by angle row
rotation_wrappers_agreement.sampling_unit: rated stimulus pair: each H1 pair contributes all of its stress angles as one cluster, so 250 pairs are resampled and never the 1750 rows

design.note: Counts and families were declared before the run. No angle was redrawn and no query swapped after seeing a result: an arm that skipped hard cases would not be comparable with the arms that ran, so every cell runs for every arm. The unrotated pose is carried as a control row (slot='control') and excluded from the rotated headline.

rotation_wrappers_retrieval.study: goal B: the rotated MPEG-7 query ranked against the stratified gallery under T0 (exact present), T1 (exact removed) and T2 (exact + rigid near-duplicates removed). T2 is the primary condition
rotation_wrappers_retrieval.metric: T2 Precision@10, true Recall@10, class MRR, NDCG@10 and Top-10 overlap with the unrotated ranking, measured over the ROTATED cells only; the 0-degree controls are published as their own view

statistics_correction.reason: d6/1 aggregated every (arm, condition) block over all 72 stored cells, including the 12 unrotated control rows, and published a Precision@10 under the name class_recall_at_k. Both are reading errors baked into the summary; neither is a new experiment.

views.rotation_only: the headline. Cells whose query was actually turned, so every rotation statistic is measured on poses that can fail.
views.unrotated_control: diagnostic only. The 0-degree poses, reported apart because a control cell asks an unrotated question: it can show the pipeline is wired correctly, and it cannot show that a wrapper survives a turn.

metric_definitions.precision_at_10: same-class share OF THE RETURNED Top-10: hits / min(k, n_returned). This is the number /1 published as class_recall_at_k, unchanged, correctly named
metric_definitions.recall_at_10: share OF THE RETAINED RELEVANT CANDIDATES that reached the Top-10: hits / n_same_class_kept for that query and condition. The denominator is per query (2, 3 or 4 under T2 here), never a constant
metric_definitions.recall_undefined: a cell with n_same_class_kept == 0 has no relevant candidate left to find, so recall_at_10 is undefined; such cells are counted in recall_at_10_undefined_cells and excluded from the mean instead of being written down as a 0.0 failure
metric_definitions.ndcg: unchanged arithmetic; ndcg_at_10_n_scored now states how many cells contributed, because NDCG@K already skipped cells that found nothing relevant
metric_definitions.class_relevance: MPEG-7 category labels are a relevance proxy for automated metrics only. They are not human similarity judgements and are never presented as such.

orientation_diagnostics.note: Statuses are the R2 wrapper's own evidence: 'isotropic-fallback' means no principal axis exists to align to, so R2 silently leaves that shape in its stored pose and is rotation-blind on it; 'sign-tie' means an axis exists but its 180-degree flip is decided by floating-point noise. E3's two counters use E3's own thresholds, which are NOT the same rule, and the disagreement column quantifies how far apart the two conventions actually put the same contour.

image_axis_convention_check.note: Angle of the RASTERISED mask's major axis after R2 canonicalised the CONTOUR. Small values mean one axis convention serves both networks; a large value means the 40x40 grid re-introduces an orientation the contour decision did not predict.
